problem: The equivalence is stated without saying s is real; for complex s the notation '< infinity' is not meaningful and the correct condition is Re s > 1 (absolute convergence).
The O / << definition omits the range of validity of the inequality, and ~ and o omit the limit x -> infinity.
corrected: $f = O(g)$ and $f \ll g$ mean $|f| \le Cg$ for some constant $C$ and all sufficiently large $x$ (or all $x$ in a stated range); $f \sim g$ means $f/g \to 1$ and $f = o(g)$ means $f/g \to 0$, as $x \to \infty$. Number theory statements are mostly sharp asymptotics with error terms.

problem: Abel's formula needs f continuously differentiable on [1, x] (and x >= 1); without it f' and the integral need not exist.
corrected: \sum_{n \le x} a_n f(n) = A(x) f(x) - \int_1^x A(t)\, f'(t)\, dt \quad (x \ge 1,\ f \in C^1[1,x])

problem: 'Zero integral around closed loops' is false on a general domain (1/z on the punctured plane has integral 2 pi i around the unit circle); the domain must be simply connected (or the loop null-homotopic).
corrected: A complex-differentiable function on a simply connected domain has zero integral around closed loops, and Cauchy's integral formula recovers its values and all derivatives from boundary values. Holomorphic functions are locally power series.

problem: The contour is unspecified; the formula holds for a positively oriented circle around a whose closed disc lies in the domain (not for an arbitrary loop).

The residue theorem is stated with no hypotheses on the function or contour (needs f holomorphic except for isolated singularities, a positively oriented simple closed contour, no singularities on it).
corrected: The integral of a meromorphic function around a positively oriented simple closed contour avoiding its poles equals $2\pi i$ times the sum of the residues inside. The argument principle and Rouché's theorem count zeros inside a contour, which is how zeros of $\zeta$ are counted.

problem: The argument principle needs f meromorphic on and inside a positively oriented simple closed contour C with no zeros or poles on C, and zeros and poles counted with multiplicity.
corrected: \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_C \frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\,dz = \#\text{zeros} - \#\text{poles} \quad (\text{inside } C, \text{ with multiplicity; } f \text{ meromorphic, no zeros or poles on } C, C \text{ positively oriented})
